activities.why: Planning around busy calendars is one of your biggest time drains.

activities.why: Letters and emails that follow a pattern are a safe first step with AI.
activities.tailoring: Draft with placeholders only and compare the result with your current template.

capstone.goal: A consistent summary of each candidate's interview, prepared for the panel, with every decision still made by people.
steps: Write the task in one sentence.
List what the AI would need, with no candidate details.
Use the five-part prompt on a made-up set of notes.
Check the summary and note what you changed.

activities.why: Calm, accurate replies to billing concerns are central to your day.
activities.tailoring: Start from a fictional complaint that resembles the ones you see most, and compare two prompt versions to see which keeps the facts straight.

activities.why: Turning rough notes into a tidy record is something you repeat after almost every contact.
activities.tailoring: Write your own made-up notes in the style you normally use, and check that nothing is lost or invented.

activities.why: Clear handovers to a supervisor save time on both sides.
activities.tailoring: Practise on a fictional case history and keep the summary to five points a supervisor can read in seconds.

capstone.goal: Ready-to-check reply drafts for the most common billing concerns, so each response starts from a strong, consistent draft.
steps: Write down the steps you follow for a typical billing concern.
Pick the step where AI saves the most time and write a prompt for it.
Turn it into a template with placeholders and test it on two made-up cases.
Share it with your team with a short note on when to use it.

activities.why: Much of your week goes on answering policy questions by email, and this is the quickest place to save time.
activities.tailoring: Use a policy extract you already rely on and a made-up staff question, and practise removing every personal detail before you prompt.

activities.why: A busy inbox is the starting point for most of your work.
activities.tailoring: Use fictional subject lines that mirror the kinds of requests you receive, and let AI suggest an order before you decide.

activities.why: Regular emails that follow the same pattern are ideal for reusable AI drafts.
activities.tailoring: Build the draft with placeholders only, then compare it with how you write these emails today.

capstone.goal: An assistant that answers routine policy questions from the handbook, so you only handle the unusual cases yourself.
steps: Write the task in one sentence.
List the handbook sections the AI would need, with no staff details.
Use the five-part prompt to answer three made-up questions.
Check each answer against the handbook and note what you corrected.

activities.why: Prioritising correspondence is where your day usually starts.

activities.why: Short briefs before meetings save reading time for you and others.

Write a prompt that turns notes into minutes and actions.
Turn it into a template and test it on two sets of made-up notes.
Save it to the team prompt library with a note on when to use it.
